transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Borealis Head of ML), Jon Erickson (Infra), Priya Singh (Product)

Summary:
Borealis is evaluating open models and deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC/on-prem) with specific concerns around multilingual support (EN/FR/ES), long context for legal/docs ingestion (~64k), and robust tool-calling for retrieval and external DB queries. They asked about quantized model options, KV cache implications, latency tradeoffs, and enterprise security (SOC2, SSO). Redwood AE/SE walked through model catalog options, 8k/32k/64k context variants, and suggested an initial hosted pilot followed by dedicated capacity or private if data residency or audit constraints require it.

Topics: model selection (Mistral, Llama, Falcon), context windows, multilingual evals, tool-calling, dedicated vs hosted, SOC2/KMS/SAML, pilot next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone thanks for taking time, this is Alex from Redwood, joined by Samira and Diego on the SE side. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya Patel: Good, thanks. We've got about 45 minutes — hoping to get into model tradeoffs and deployment options.
[00:10] Alex Mercer: Perfect. Quick agenda: understand your workloads, talk model families and context windows, go over tool-calling and infra, and agree next steps.
[00:18] Jon Erickson: Quick note on infra, we run a hybrid cloud right now. Our docs live in AWS S3, some PHI-ish records are in GCP project, and we have strict audit and retention rules. So private or VPC options are interesting.
[00:31] Samira Khan: Noted. Can I ask what your primary latency SLO is for user-facing features? 100-200ms per token, or is end-to-end latency more important?
[00:39] Priya Singh: End-to-end. For chat it's okay to be a bit higher, but for inline assistant responses in our product we target sub-2s for short prompts. For long-doc summarization latency is less critical.
[00:50] Maya Patel: For scale, expect 50–200 QPS for embeddings/semantic search during peak.
[00:56] Alex Mercer: Good. On model choices, we've seen teams pick Mistral-style models for instruction tasks, Falcon variants for cost-sensitive throughput, and Llama-family for fine-tuning/weight-sharing. For long context we can suggest 32k and 64k variants; there are also emerging 128k options but those have higher memory and cost.
[01:15] Maya Patel: We need multilingual — EN, FR, ES — and good behavior on code-switching. Any models you recommend out of the box?
[01:22] Samira Khan: Mistral XXL does well on multilingual general tasks, and some Llama2 70B variants have been extended with multi-lingual fine-tunes. Falcon-40B Constellation (noisily named in our docs) is cost efficient but tends to drop on less common French idioms. We should run your sample prompts to validate.
[01:42] Jon Erickson: How does context length affect caching and KV-store? We're planning to use prefix caching for repeated queries.
[01:47] Diego Ramos: Great question. Longer context increases KV cache use and memory. Redwood's runtime will automatically route longer sequences to nodes with larger KV capacity. For dedicated you can pick instance classes optimized for long context which reduces token cost by enabling larger batch packing. But you'll trade off latency if the batch is large.
[02:05] Maya Patel: We have legal docs up to 80k tokens — need accurate summarization. Do you support 128k contexts?
[02:11] Samira Khan: We do have 128k-capable stacks in our private/on-prem offering, and some hosted models exposed in Beta get up to 128k. For production at scale, Dedicated with tuned kernels and quantization is recommended. Note: quantization for 128k scenarios can be tricky; we recommend 8-bit quant profiles we validated for your model family.
[02:31] Priya Singh: What about tool-calling? We need retrieval-augmented generation with tool-calls to our internal DBs and a ticketing system.
[02:37] Alex Mercer: Redwood supports structured tool-calling and function calling patterns, streaming back tool outputs, and we can enforce sandboxing. For private deployments you can host adapters close to data and use our routing proxies to keep data in-region.
[02:51] Jon Erickson: Security: we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, and optional HSM. Can you tick those off?
[02:58] Samira Khan: Yes — hosted has SOC2 and we support SAML/SSO and audit logs. For KMS/HSM integrations, Dedicated and Private have richer integrations (customer-managed keys, HSM options). We'll share our security whitepaper. Also note deletion and retention hooks to satisfy retention policies.
[03:16] Maya Patel: Latency vs cost: if we go to dedicated reserved capacity what are the economics vs hosted burst?
[03:22] Diego Ramos: Hosted is easiest to start but unit cost per token is higher and noisy in peak. Dedicated reserves GPU pools with predictable throughput and lower unit costs; there are commit terms. You can also use hybrid: host baseline traffic and failover to dedicated. We'll include numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:38] Maya Patel: Any vendor lock-in? If we start hosted and then want private, how much rework?
[03:43] Alex Mercer: Minimal — one of Redwood's differentiators is consistent API and config across hosted, dedicated, and private. You'll mainly need to move data and keys; model versions and prompt logic stay the same. Some infra automation will need adjustment but not model code.
[03:56] Priya Singh: We need deterministic outputs for some compliance features; do you support model pinning and fixed rollouts?
[04:02] Samira Khan: Yes — you can pin model versions and control rollouts with canaries/A-B. We also have quality monitors and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[04:12] Jon Erickson: On the technical bench, could we run a latency run with our prompts? We want to see tail latency for 32k vs 64k contexts, and compare quantized 8-bit vs float16.
[04:20] Diego Ramos: Absolutely. For the bench we'll need sample prompts and a spec for distribution (prompt length percentiles). We'll spin up nodes in Dedicated staging for apples-to-apples.
[04:31] Maya Patel: Will you be able to simulate multilingual traffic?
[04:34] Samira Khan: Yes — include language breakdown in the dataset and we'll include language-specific metrics (accuracy, hallucination rates).
[04:42] Priya Singh: Any concerns about hallucinations when chaining tool calls? We need reliable citation to source docs.
[04:48] Alex Mercer: Tool-calling with retrieval + grounding reduces hallucinations. We'll recommend best practices: short grounding snippets, confidence thresholds, and verification steps. We can also route uncertain outputs to a human-in-the-loop flow.
[05:00] Maya Patel: For private deployments, what are typical lead times and install footprint?
[05:04] Samira Khan: Private VPC can be weeks depending on network approvals; on-prem is longer — often 6–10 weeks including security review. Footprint depends on model sizes and context needs — we'll share a sizing estimate.
[05:16] Jon Erickson: Do you have reference architecture docs for hybrid routing and fallback?
[05:20] Alex Mercer: Yes — we'll attach the hybrid-routing doc. It shows policy-based routing by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when instances are constrained.
[05:30] Maya Patel: Any gotchas with embeddings for multilingual? We're doing semantic search across EN/FR/ES.
[05:36] Diego Ramos: Use language-agnostic embedding models or run per-language encoders if you need higher fidelity. We'll test both approaches in the pilot. Also note normalization steps — stopword lists differ per language which affects recall.
[05:49] Priya Singh: Who's the contact for legal/security to push contracts?
[05:53] Alex Mercer: I'll loop in our security and legal; we'll send the security pack and sample SOC2 report.
[05:59] Maya Patel: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[06:02] Alex Mercer: Recap: Alex shares pricing/model perf spreadsheet and security docs; Samira schedules technical deep dive to run latency benches on 32k and 64k contexts; Borealis to share prompt sets and SAML metadata. We aim to have initial bench results in one week.
[06:20] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Any questions from your side?
[06:23] Jon Erickson: No further questions.
[06:24] Alex Mercer: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

End of transcript.
